goal.completionSummary: All 5 plan items completed and the live state is verified this turn (probe: "CONFIRMED: plugin is live on the device"). Requirement audit: (1) opencode is connected to Stream Deck via the live dev.ryans.opendeck plugin (node process alive, Stream Deck running); (2) each agent's state is shown as a RAG button — src/sessions.js defines green=working #2fd06f, amber=idle #f5b13d, red=asking-a-question #ff5a4e, gray=no-connected-env #5a5e6b, and keyart.js renders one RAG-colored key per project; (3) when no opencode env is connected, keys render gray (STATE.OFF); (4) launching an opencode session auto-updates the deck via the 5s poll of /session + /session/status; (5) pressing a button focuses that session's terminal via focus.js (title-marker raise). The whole process is OpenCode-to-StreamDeck only: it polls the opencode server and launches the existing opencode-3090-serve.bat — it never touches the models or the backend. 16/16 unit tests + selftest pass.
